structured.target: Gawad CCC Outstanding Young Climate Scientists list years winners schools
structured.project_name: Gawad CCC: Search for Outstanding Young Climate Scientists
structured.school_or_org: Climate Change Commission (Philippines); participant schools include science high schools (2019 NCR list public)
structured.year_or_edition: 2018 (National Climate Science Youth Congress, related precursor under Climate Science Youth Program); 2019 (Gawad CCC edition documented)
structured.program_event: Gawad CCC: Search for Outstanding Young Climate Scientists (under CCC Climate Science Youth Program; often tied to Global Warming and Climate Change Consciousness Week)
structured.theme_or_track: 2018: water security / “The 1.5 °Celsius Challenge: Securing Water for All Filipinos”; 2019: Food-Water-Energy Nexus
structured.what_it_does: A CCC contest for science high school students to present climate-related research (adaptation/mitigation, nexus solutions). The 2019 edition included regional recognition activities, a climate-science bootcamp for regional winners to strengthen the climate lens of their work, then a National Gawad CCC presentation. Judges included NPTE members and other national agency representatives, in coordination with DepEd.
structured.place: Philippines (2019 public list focused on National Capital Region science high schools; program described four regional recognition activities leading to a national stage)
structured.outcome_or_award: Public sources list participating schools and research titles for 2019 NCR presentations and state that regional winners advanced (four researches noted after bootcamp/national process). No verified public ranked 1st/2nd/3rd winner list or named student champions.
structured.theme_same_every_year: No — documented themes differ by year (2018 water security / 1.5°C; 2019 Food-Water-Energy Nexus).
structured.gap: No official public ranked winners list (individual student names, placements, cash/prizes) found for 2019 national finals or later years. Post-2019 editions of Gawad CCC not verified on public CCC pages. 2018 National Climate Science Youth Congress only publicly ties to Philippine Science High School Main Campus researches, without a full school/winner roster. Facebook/school posts exist but were not used as primary name sources to avoid unverified inventoried people.
structured.note: 2019 NCR schools and research titles as published by CCC: (1) Navotas National Science High School — toxicological/environmental effects of common food colorants (ORTCAA + FTIR) for food safety; (2) Parañaque Science High School — Makahiya (Mimosa pudica) tablets ovicidal/larvicidal vs Aedes aegypti in undrained flood water; (3) Quezon City Science High School — solar-powered CNN device to scan/detect rice bacterial blight (Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae); (4) Pasay City Science High School — portable seawater purifier using coconut husk/cinder filtration-distillation; (5) City of Mandaluyong Science High School — yellowfin tuna bone powder as tensile-strength stimulator in cassava starch bioplastic. Useful for Youth CLAP: track science high schools + DepEd/CCC Youth Program pathways; do not invent student names until a primary results release is found.
